Alex.note: As the Sphinx I name a farm role and learn who holds it. Farm roles in play are Eagle, Hawk, Kookaburra, Tit. I'll name Eagle.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia Floofer. Hugging Alex blocks an information role that could threaten us during the night.

Casey.note: As Tit I can only gain an egg by guessing a role correctly. Pigeon is a common role, so I'll visit Finley and guess Pigeon.

Drew.note: I'm Farm Hawk. Ellis leads on points and has been erratic in the last two rounds, so I'll check them for Meowfia.

Ellis.note: As Kookaburra on Farm, I'll visit Alex to learn their role, since Alex is a strong rival and their claims have been consistent.

Finley.note: As Farm Eagle, I'll visit Ellis, the suspect with the unexplained +2, to learn their visitors and gain eggs.

Alex.feeling: Tense and a bit precarious: I'm the Meowfia Sphinx, my unchanged nest made Blair's Hawk claim look false, and the table is now throwing at Blair.

Blair.feeling: Tense and going badly: I'm actually Meowfia, four players are throwing at me, and my Hawk story rests on an egg count that doesn't add up.

Casey.feeling: Messy and contradictory: Blair's Hawk visit to Alex doesn't match Alex's unchanged Turkey nest, so I'm fairly suspicious of Blair.

Drew.feeling: Round 3 is tense: Blair's Hawk story contradicts the unchanged nests, and the table has mostly converged on them, though Ellis's confused report and lost eggs leave some doubt.

Ellis.feeling: Round 3 is messy: Blair's Hawk and Turkey stories don't match, and the table is moving to throw at Blair, but my own Kookaburra report was confused, so I'm relying on other players' claims.

Finley.feeling: Tense and confusing: several players contradict each other, and the table is closing in on Blair.

Alex.note: Four Farm players are throwing at Blair, so my single card won't change the outcome. I'll throw one low card at Drew to keep my higher cards.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia and the vote is on me, so I'll throw low cards at Ellis, the leader and a likely Farm player, to add a vote against the Farm side.

Casey.note: Blair is the consensus target and their Turkey/Hawk story fails. I'm throwing my lowest card, C6, at Blair.

Drew.note: Blair is the consensus target and their Hawk claim fails. I'll throw my Wild, a single vote with no value at risk.

Ellis.note: Blair is the consensus target, so I'll throw my low D7 at Blair.

Finley.note: Keeping the vote on Blair with my Wild W1.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle's rule was easy to misread: I first thought it counted visitors to me, when it counts visitors to the player I visit. Confused reports also made several claims hard to check.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when Drew's shifting Hawk story fell apart and the table lined up a clean CAW and vote on them.
Alex.change: Make role claims and visit results easier to verify, perhaps by having the Storyteller confirm each visit's effect publicly.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I was the Sphinx, a Meowfia, and I backed the Farm push on Blair while throwing at Drew, a Farm player. I would instead have thrown at a Farm player who was building a case against Blair and kept my cards out of the throw.

Blair.confusing: The Floofer's hug and the Turkey's egg rule were hard to reason about, since a blocked visit looks identical to no visit. I also couldn't tell whether a Turkey's "no egg" meant nobody came or that its role was blocked.
Blair.fun: Round 2's Eagle reveal was satisfying: visiting Ellis showed Casey as a visitor, and it helped the table converge on Drew, who was Meowfia.
Blair.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about blocked or hugged roles, so a Turkey or Eagle player can tell whether a no-egg result came from nobody visiting or from a block.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw three cards at Ellis, a Farm player, on thin evidence, and I should have kept my throw small until the claims were clearer.

Casey.confusing: Roles and claims reshuffle every round, so a player's earlier claim is easy to misread, and confused reports make egg counts unreliable. I could not tell which dawn reports to trust.
Casey.fun: Round 2, when Drew's Hawk story kept shifting and the table converged on Drew, who turned out to be a Meowfia Floofer.
Casey.change: Make the Storyteller's dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so the table can verify claims without relying on guesswork.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I threw at Blair, a Farm Kookaburra, based on a confused report; I should have questioned Finley, who claimed Owl and then Turkey and was the real Sphinx Meowfia.

Drew.confusing: The Round 2 Meowfia claim: I lied as the Floofer, and it was hard to track whether Alex's Owl report or Blair's Eagle claim was real since roles reshuffle each round. The egg-gain logic for Eagle and Turkey was also easy to misread.
Drew.fun: Round 3, when my Hawk visit to Ellis and Finley's Eagle report lined up and the table converged on Blair, who turned out to be the Meowfia Floofer.
Drew.change: Make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, so claims are easier to check without guessing.
Drew.regret: In Round 2 I lied about visiting Finley and then shifted to Alex, which made my Meowfia role easy to spot. I would stick to one consistent story and throw at a clearer target instead of Ellis.

Ellis.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion was hard to read: a confused report can be wrong about both the count and the role, so I couldn't trust my own visit results. Roles changing every round made earlier claims hard to track.
Ellis.fun: Round 2 went well: Drew's Hawk story kept shifting, and the table converged on a correct eggsecution. Round 3's Turkey-egg check against Alex's unchanged nest was a good way to catch Blair's lie.
Ellis.change: I'd make it clearer when a dawn report is confused, such as showing which parts of it are wrong. That would reduce wasted suspicion on honest players.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw at Blair, who was Farm, and sided with the accusation after Casey and Drew pushed it. I should have pressed Finley harder, since Finley was the Meowfia Sphinx and vague about their role.

Finley.confusing: Round 1 confusion was mine: the Sphinx's "learn who they are" is one visit to one player, so I could only confirm one identity, and I didn't use it well. Several "confused" reports also made it hard to tell which dawn counts to trust.
Finley.fun: Round 2's throws piled onto Drew after the caw, and the Floofer's hidden role made the Hawk story collapse under the table's questions. It was a clean, tense read.
Finley.change: I would make the Sphinx's learned roles and visit results clearer in the dawn report, so Meowfia players can plan their claims without guessing what they're allowed to know.
Finley.regret: I bluffed an Owl claim in Round 1 with an invented visit to Casey and a muddled "Hawk-type" line, which made me look evasive. I would stick to a short, consistent story, or stay quiet, instead of inventing details I then had to defend.

review.title: Wild Throws, Easy Votes
review.headline: Farm lynched its own Kookaburra, then twice caught Meowfia by contradiction.
review.summary: Round 1 ended with Farm eggsecuting a confused Kookaburra while the lone Meowfia Sphinx bluffed an Owl and won. In rounds 2 and 3 the Meowfia were caught quickly, by a shifting Hawk story and by a Turkey-egg contradiction. Ellis won the game by banking mid-value cards on winning throws. The Meowfia had little power to disrupt anything.

rounds.recap: Blair was confused, so the Kookaburra report was wrong and the +2 eggs looked suspicious. The table piled on Blair, a Farm player. Finley, the lone Meowfia Sphinx, stayed vague, then bluffed Owl and won while throwing a Wild.

Drew, a Floofer, claimed Hawk and named Finley as his target. Finley the Turkey said nobody came, and Drew switched to Alex. Blair's Eagle report backed Casey's Hawk claim. All five others threw at Drew and Farm won.

Blair (Floofer) claimed Hawk, which clashed with Drew's real Hawk and Finley's Eagle report. Alex (Sphinx) claimed Turkey with an unchanged nest, which made Blair's visit look impossible. Blair was eggsecuted and Alex, though Meowfia, was never suspected.

highlights.text: Finley the Turkey flatly said nobody visited, which exposed Drew's Hawk visit to Finley as a lie.
Casey spotted that a Turkey visit should have given Blair an egg, and the table collapsed Blair's Hawk claim.
Finley's Eagle report that Drew alone visited Ellis cleanly verified the real Hawk.
Finley bluffed an unclaimed Owl with a no-change story and a Farm player was eggsecuted.

confusions.what: Said Alex claimed Ellis visited him, when Alex said Ellis visited Blair.
Thought the Eagle gains eggs from visitors to the Eagle, not to the target.
Said Blair's confusion proved Blair wrong about Casey, though Blair's own confused report was the unreliable part.
Claimed 'Hawk-type', which is not a role.
Said Blair's Eagle claim conflicted with last round's Kookaburra claim. Roles are redealt each round.
Claimed Turkey eggs can be blocked by a hug, but Alex was the one hugged and Blair's real visit never happened.

Claimed Turkey with a nest that looked unchanged, but a Turkey's claim also made Blair's Hawk visit impossible, which hurt Alex's own partner. Alex also said a Hawk would get an egg for visiting Meowfia, revealing knowledge.
Said Alex had an Eagle/Owl switch in the survey, but Alex only claimed Owl.

worked: Turkey: Finley's flat 'nobody visited me' made a clean, checkable fact that exposed Drew's lie in round 2.
Eagle and Falcon visit reports: Finley's Eagle result in round 3 verified Drew's Hawk visit and gave real deduction.
Confused status: it made Blair's and Ellis's reports truly unreliable, which led to a good argument in round 1.
Throw-value choice: Ellis banking H5, D7 and the like on winning throws made the endgame about score, not only the vote.
problems: Votes pile on one target fast. In rounds 2 and 3 five players threw at the same Meowfia with no real doubt. Consider fewer clear tells or scarcer information.
Meowfia are weak. Floofer hugged a player with no effect in two rounds, and Sphinx info was never used. Give cats a way to act on the day or reward Meowfia more.
Meowfia winning round 1 scored nothing for Finley, since a Wild was thrown. Winning as Meowfia depends on throwing real cards, and nobody wants to.

Players threw Wilds and low cards almost every time, so the score race was decided by who happened to be on the winning team. Ellis's lead came from one +5 and +7 banked. Consider making thrown value matter more.

Confusion and visit wording are hard for the players, who repeatedly misread Eagle, Turkey and Hawk. The rules need worked examples, and the app should show hug effects clearly ('no effect at tier 50' is opaque).
